name: MapReduce
description: MapReduce is a programming model and implementation for processing large data sets in a distributed parallel manner. It abstracts parallelization, fault tolerance, data distribution, and load balancing from developers, allowing them to focus on data processing logic.
real_world_examples: Word count on massive text corpora
how_it_works: The model has two phases: Map and Reduce. Map takes input key-value pairs and produces intermediate key-value pairs. The framework groups intermediate values by key and passes them to Reduce, which aggregates values for each key. The runtime handles partitioning, sorting, and parallel execution across clusters.

complexity.time: O(n/p) parallel time where n=input size, p=processors; total work O(n log n) for sorting
complexity.space: O(n) distributed across nodes; O(1) per mapper/reducer locally

pseudocode_or_diagram_description: Map(k1, v1) → list(k2, v2): process input record, emit intermediate pairs. Reduce(k2, list(v2)) → list(k3, v3): aggregate values for key, emit output. Framework: partition by key hash, sort, group, and send to reducers. Fault tolerance through task re-execution on failure.
